description: Three unreconciled state vocabularies describe indexes and the Index Service, and no page names a scheme or maps one onto another. (1) The SQL++ DDL reference gives an index's lifecycle: scheduled for creation, deferred, building, pending, online, offline, abridged. (2) manage-indexes.md gives the Index Service's state on a node, reported as an index's `status`: ready, pause, warmup, 'n mutations remaining'. (3) storage-modes.md uses two further words in two sentences, at two different levels, and defines neither: 'the indexer goes into the Paused mode on that node; and although the indexes remain in `Active` state, traffic is routed away from the node' plus 'the indexer goes into Active mode again on that node' (a NODE state), and 'these indexes remain in the `Warmup` state until all information has been read into memory: then, final updates are made with the indexes in `Active` state' (an INDEX state - applying to an index a word vocabulary 2 applies to a node). `Active` appears in neither of the two enumerated vocabularies. A reader cannot tell whether `Active` is what vocabulary 2 calls `ready`, or what vocabulary 1 calls `online`, or a third thing; nor whether an index in `Warmup` is what vocabulary 1 calls `building`.
note:
Two of the three are promoted as separate enums and stay separate: `index-state` (lifecycle of an index, from the DDL reference) and `indexer-node-state` (condition of a node's Index Service). Round 12 refused to merge those two and round 16 reaffirms the refusal, because the value sets do not match and no page reconciles them - the refusal is the finding. The third vocabulary is not promoted at all: 'Active' and 'Warmup' as used here have no defining sentence anywhere in the corpus, and minting an enum for them would be inventing the scheme rather than extracting it. This is the case that would be settled by one sentence from an SME, which is why it is filed here.
ROUND 17 ADDS A THIRD AND FOURTH SENSE, AND ONE PIECE OF EVIDENCE THAT KILLS THE SIMPLEST RECONCILIATION. The simplest fix would be that these vocabularies are one enum seen from different angles. storage-modes.md rules it out by using two of the words at once, of two different subjects, in one sentence: 'the indexer goes into the Paused mode on that node. Although the indexes remain in `Active` state, traffic is routed away from the node.' Paused (the indexer) and Active (the indexes) hold SIMULTANEOUSLY, so they cannot be members of one value set. `Active` appears in neither promoted enum.
Also new: index-replication.md introduces a third sense of 'index state' meaning the index's current CONTENTS rather than its lifecycle position or its node's condition; and index-lifecycle.md - a page titled 'Index Lifecycle' - names ZERO states in either tree, modelling four activities with phases instead. So the lifecycle documentation and the registry are not disagreeing about values; they are modelling different things, and nothing in the corpus joins phases to states.
